content.text: Atherosclerotic disease of the arteries of the lower extremities
– MC sxs (lower extremity pain w/ ambulation)
*Leriche’s Syndrome: triad of buttock/thigh claudication + impotence + ↓ femoral pulses
: in advanced disease; MC at night & relieved w/ foot dependency
– muscle atrophy, thin/shiny skin, hair loss, thickened nails cool limbs, areas of necrosis; usually no edema
(0.50 is severe); rest pain if <0.4 (normal is 1-1.2)
•>1.2 🡪 possible noncompressible (calcified) vessels – may lead to a false reading
– usually only performed if revascularization is planned
smoking cessation associated w/ greatest benefit
most effective medical therapy; aspirin, clopidogrel, pentoxifylline
: percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (first line revascularization procedure) bypass grafts, endarterectomy (last line)
– rapidly developing or sudden decrease in limb perfusion
MC in the superficial femoral or popliteal artery
late finding associated w/ a worse prognosis
); sxs usually distal to the occlusion
Decreased capillary refill, decreased or absent pulses, cool temperature
An immediately threatened limb may undergo further evaluation & treatment in a surgical suite
, endarterectomy; thrombolytic therapy or percutaneous angioplasty
Supportive: pain control, fluid resuscitation, UFH
